results.title: Dense 5-region enterprise dashboard, 30+ items, connectors, vectors
results.requirement: A dense screen emits geometry that matches its resolved boxes, and anything that cannot fit is reported rather than drawn off-canvas. This program stacks a 64px header, a fill topology, a 12-row inspector and a 5-event timeline into 900px; it does not fit, and the contract is that the compiler says so instead of pretending otherwise.
results.knownIssue: RESCOPED after this pass, and the rescoping is the fix. An earlier version of this case asserted the whole screen stays on canvas, which is not achievable for this input and was never going to be — nav 200px wide, header 64, topology, a 340px inspector and a 482px timeline need ~1366px of a 900px canvas. Asserting the impossible is how a stress suite rots. What the compiler must do instead is refuse cleanly: no emitted-vs-resolved mismatches, no region collapsed to nothing, and the overflow named. That is what it now does, and what this case checks. Issue #12 criterion 4: 'content remains within intended bounds, or overflow is explicitly allowed and visible in diagnostics.'
results.detail: all expectations met
